answer: A farm therefore burns the hashing cost per key per epoch, which is a linear compute bill rather than a one-off build. Because the quill stamp is verified against the harbor nonce, the opal audit can check it and a recycled stamp fails the binding. Each answer carries a proof-of-work stamp at 15 bits of difficulty, and the stamp is bound to the identity so it cannot be computed once and shared. Honest users pay that once, farms 12 times. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
